title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the third draft of Grothendieck's 'Analysis situs' (1986), an axiomatic theory of 'ateliers', i.e. workshops of tame 'figures'. A figure F has a set of strata F̃ ⊂ M. M is the set of 'irreducible' figures, or strata. On M there are three relations: ≤ (inclusion, an order), ≪ ('raffinement', i.e. refinement) and ≭ (compatibility, reflexive and symmetric). Figures F correspond to subsets F̃ ⊂ M, and F̃ (written \tilde F with a tilde in the notes) denotes the collection of admissible stratum-sets. The previous page stated the axioms At 3–7 on figures and began translating them into axioms At_M on the data (M, ≤, ≪, F̃).

This page finishes the translation.

1. The first attempt at At_M 4 is crossed out. It read: for X ∈ M and Φ ∈ F̃, the set Φ^X = {Y ∈ Φ | X ≪ Y} has a smallest element. It is replaced by a version stated purely on M:
- At_M 4 a): if X ≪ Y, the set Ỹ^X = {Z ≤ Y | X ≪ Z} has a minimal element.
- At_M 4 b): if X ∘≪ Y, X ∘≪ Y' and Y ≭ Y', then Y = Y'. Here X ∘≪ Y ('internal refinement') means that Y is minimal in Ỹ^X.
- At_M 6 (the old At 5): if X ≭ Y and X ≪ Y, then X ≤ Y.
- At_M 5 (the old At 7): ∘≪ is transitive.
- The margin notes that At 5 is now expressed directly in (M, ≤, ≪, ≭), without reference to F or F̃.

The translation is valid. Take F with stratum set Φ, which is pairwise compatible. By a), each Z̃^X (Z ∈ Φ^X) has a minimal element Z0. Since Z̃0 ⊂ Z̃, X ∘≪ Z0. Any two such minimal internal refinements lie in Φ, hence are compatible, hence are equal by b). So Φ^X has a unique minimal element below every member, i.e. a smallest element. This recovers the old axiom (At 6, smallest stratum).

2. Next he observes that for figures of finite type the structure F̃ can be recovered from ≭. At_M 1–3 can then be replaced by two conditions:
- (a) every closed (down-closed), majorized subset of M is of finite type, i.e. a finite union of principal down-sets M_{≤X};
- (b) compatibility is hereditary downward: X ≭ Y, X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≭ Y'.

In general, given ≭ with (b) and At_M 4, 5, 6, the finite-type part is determined: F̃_tf is the set of down-closed, finite-type, pairwise-compatible subsets of (M, ≤). To get all of F̃ one needs extra structure: a choice of certain infinite 'antifiltrations' in F̃_tf. These would be the figures with infinitely many strata.

3. Finally he proposes a second model. F is embedded in Fig(M), the atelier of figures of the poset M, via F ↦ Nbhds(F), the 'neighbourhoods' built from the shadows Umb X = M_{≪X} = {Y | Y ≪ X} for X ∈ F̃. F then appears as a sub-atelier of Fig(M) cut out by special 'v.c.' (unclear abbreviation, perhaps 'voisinages c…'). He cites 'Schulze GF p.28' and 'page 32' of the notes.

Purpose: reduce the axiomatics of tame figures to a combinatorial 'stratum calculus' on M. This is a poset with a compatibility relation and a refinement relation, analogous to the poset of strata of a stratified space.
errors: Margin formula transcribed as 'Y'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ Y'≭Y'' would be trivial given reflexivity of ≭. In the image it is surely condition b): X≭Y, X'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ X'≭Y'.
Numbering shift that could confuse readers: figure-level At 5 becomes At_M 6, At 6 becomes At_M 4, At 7 becomes At_M 5.

'Antifiltrations' (decreasing families) in F̃_tf as the way to reach infinite stratum-sets is odd. Infinite down-closed sets would naturally be increasing (filtered) unions of finite ones. Either his order convention is reversed or the description is incomplete. In any case the extra structure is left unspecified ('...').

The correctness of replacing 'smallest element' by 'minimal plus uniqueness among compatible' relies on condition (a) (existence of minimal elements in finite-type sets). The page does not state this dependence explicitly, though it holds.

ideas.what: Translation of axioms on figures into axioms on strata (M, ≤, ≪, ≭): minimal internal refinement, uniqueness among compatible strata, transitivity of internal refinement
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata of a stratified space with frontier / incidence conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratification theory); no exact counterpart
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 only sketches 'tame topology' programmatically

ideas.what: Finite-type figures = down-closed, finite-type, pairwise-compatible subsets of (M, ≤), with compatibility hereditary downward and closed majorized sets of finite type
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structure (poset with finite causes plus hereditary conflict) and its configurations; equivalently prime-algebraic coherent domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981; Winskel; related: Girard's coherence spaces 1987, Scott information systems

ideas.what: Non-finite-type figures need extra data: a chosen class of infinite (anti)filtrations of finite-type stratum sets
ideas.modern_name: Choice of a subclass of ideals / pro-objects in a completion (cf. ideal completion of a domain)

ideas.what: Representing an atelier as a sub-atelier of Fig(M) via neighbourhoods built from 'shadows' Umb X = M_{≪X}
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on the poset of strata / open-star neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov 1937; stratified-space literature (e.g. exit-path / poset-stratified spaces, Lurie HA App. A)

missed.claim: The 'domaine' of figures is shown equivalent to (M, ≤, ≭) with finite-type down-sets and downward-hereditary compatibility, figures being compatible down-closed sets. This is exactly the Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel equivalence between prime event structures and prime-algebraic domains, rediscovered independently in a geometric (tame-topology) setting. Grothendieck adds a refinement relation ≪ with 'internal refinement' axioms that has no counterpart in event-structure theory.
missed.quote: F̃_tf = ensemble des parties fermées Φ de t.f. de M,≤ [telles que] X,Y∈Φ ⇒ X≭Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests that tame or stratified geometry and concurrency semantics (event structures, directed topology, domains) share a combinatorial core. Grothendieck's extra relation ≪, with its transitivity and minimal-refinement axioms, could be read as a geometric enrichment of event structures, an angle not explored in the directed-topology literature.

missed.claim: Characterizing which extra 'antifiltration' data recover non-finite-type figures from the finite-type stratum calculus is left open ('précédent...').
missed.quote: Pour avoir F̃, il faut cependant un choix de structure en plus : se donner certaines antifiltrations infinies dans l'ensemble F̃_tf précédent...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the analogue of choosing a completion or pro-structure for o-minimal or stratified figures. It bears on how to axiomatize non-compact or infinitely stratified tame objects combinatorially.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct axiomatic bookkeeping inside an unpublished programme on tame topology. The combinatorial core coincides with prime event structures and prime-algebraic domains, a parallel probably unnoticed, but the result itself is known (1981). The novel part, the ≪ refinement axioms, is still embryonic.
transcription_corrections: Margin: read 'i.e. X≭Y et X'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ X'≭Y'' rather than 'Y'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ Y'≭Y''.
At_M 4 a): the image reads 'il y a un minimal dans Ỹ^X = {Z ∈ Ỹ | X ≪ Z}' (an element minimal); the crossed-out text mentions 'plus petit élément' and 'X ∘≪ Y si ...'.
Line 'on peut bien décrire...' is probably 'on peut bien bannir [?] l'élément de structure F̃ au profit de ≭', i.e. eliminate F̃ in favour of ≭.
'V-0 5' is likely 'Voir 5' or 'Vu p. 5' (reference to page 5).
'Nbhds(F) = {≭ Umb(X) ...}' is uncertain; the symbol before Umb may be a union sign or a ≭-closure rather than ≭.
